note: Sports XR game studio (NFL Pro Era), Miami. The company's release (PR Newswire, 2024-02-05) announces a $20M Series A led by GV, with Dream Sports, Wise Ventures and Alumni Ventures and existing backers (LeBron James, Drake, Maverick Carter), GV not among them; the firm's listing first carries the company in 2024. An earlier $5.2M raise (Refresh Miami headline, August 2021) is not tied to GV. Private; no priced round near $1B. Not in the momentum slice (gaming).

Resale marketplace for sneakers and streetwear, Detroit. GV co-led the $44M Series B with Battery Ventures (the company's release, PR Newswire, 2018-09-13); the firm's case study also gives 'First Round: Series B', invested 2018. Series C $110M at $1B (June 2019, DST Global, General Atlantic, GGV; headlines). Mark: the $255M round of April 2021 at more than $3.8B (Reuters as quoted by Wikipedia); no later priced round found, so the 2021 mark stands, flagged stale. Pinned from the unicorn list's name match to a cited event; aligned with Battery's row (Detroit, Growth).

Sensors and software that predict produce ripeness to cut food waste. The $8M Series A (June 2022) was led by Millennium New Horizons with Google Ventures, Rich Products Ventures, Mark Cuban, Union Labs, Catapult and Yamaha (Global AgInvesting); the $3.3M seed of May 2020 was co-led by Catapult and Yamaha with Mark Cuban and Union Labs and names no GV, so GV entered at the Series A (the firm's listing first carries it in 2022). Moved from Philadelphia to Seattle in 2022 (Business Journals headline); the company's own site gives 119 Pine St, Seattle and is live. General Catalyst's row still says Philadelphia: this row holds the fresher cited address.

Payments infrastructure, dual-headquartered in South San Francisco and Dublin (Wikipedia). The pre-filled 'acquired' is a Wikidata name join and is disputed: Stripe is private and operating. Mark: the employee tender at $159B announced 2026-02-24 (Stripe's own newsroom). Entry: the firm's case study gives 'First Round: Series D', invested 2016, so Growth. City follows the majority of sibling books (South San Francisco; three books say San Francisco). Not in the momentum slice (listed since 2016).

AI video generation, London (Synthesia Limited, Wikipedia). The pre-filled 'acquired' and CZ are a Wikidata join on the one-word name (a Czech namesake) and are disputed. Entry: the firm's case study gives 'First Round: Series B' (invested 2021) and its /ai list 'Invested 2021-11'; Wikipedia: the $50M Series B of December 2021 was led by Kleiner Perkins and GV. GV re-invested in 2023 and December 2024 and led the $200M Series E at $4B in January 2026 (Silicon Republic). Momentum check 2026-09-28: the January 2026 Series E is the latest priced round found. Aligned with Accel's row ($4B, 2026-01, London, GB).

Frontier AI lab founded by Mira Murati, San Francisco (Wikipedia). The firm's /ai list gives one round, 'Invested 2025-07', and the only round the company closed that month is the $2B seed at $12B led by Andreessen Horowitz (TechCrunch, 2025-07-15), so the entry is named from the record (model, medium): TechCrunch's investor list does not name GV. Mark pinned to that round (the unicorn list's figure, now cited). Momentum check 2026-09-28: talks at $50B (November 2025) and a reported $1B round at $40B led by Accel (September 2026) are not closed rounds, so no later mark. Entry 2025-07 is inside 24 months: censored. Aligned with a16z's row (Seed, $12B, San Francisco).

Network intelligence platform, San Francisco. Wikipedia: Sequoia led the 2011 Series A, Sutter Hill the 2014 Series B, and 'In 2016, Tenaya Capital and GV joined a Series C round' ($35M); GV then led the $50M Series D (February 2019). The firm's own post (2020-05-28) says its partner first met the founders in 2015, consistent with a 2016 entry. Acquired by Cisco (announced May 2020, closed August 2020, reported near $1B; the firm's exit line 'Acquired by Cisco, 2020'), so below_1b by the acquired-row rule. Aligned with Sutter Hill and Sequoia (acquired, San Francisco).

Subscription news newsletter and media company, New York. Wikipedia: an $8M Series B in June 2016, then 'On March 15, 2018, theSkimm raised a $12 million funding round led by Google Ventures'; the firm's listing first carries the company in 2018, so GV entered after the Series B: Growth. Acquired by Everyday Health Group (Ziff Davis) in March 2025 (Wikipedia; Axios and Inc. headlines; the firm's exit line 'Acquired by Everyday Health, 2025').

Agentic AI platform for hospital and physician-group finance (healthcare's 'financial operating system'). The firm's own post (2026-03-11): 'GV is leading the Series A for Translucent' and 'welcome them to the GV family', with the team in NYC; the company's site: 'We raised a $27M Series A led by GV'. The /ai list gives 'Invested 2026-03'. Healthcare vertical software, so Healthcare & Bio. The company's $7M seed of August 2025 (FinSMEs and Business Wire headlines) names no GV, and the post presents the Series A as GV's arrival. Momentum check 2026-09-28 (Google News for the company): the March 2026 Series A is the latest round.

TCR-engineered T cell therapies (NASDAQ: TCRX), Waltham MA. The S-1's related-party table: 'Entities affiliated with GV' bought 5,263,158 Series A shares for $5.0M in the Series A sold in June and December 2018, then Series B (2019) and Series C (January 2021) shares. Market cap $23.04M on 2026-09-28 (stockanalysis.com), replacing the June 2025 float.

Restaurant point-of-sale and payments platform (NYSE: TOST), Boston. The company's release (PR Newswire, 2016-01-05): a $30M Series B 'led by Bessemer Venture Partners with participation from GV', and 'Toast looks forward to working with Rich Miner ... general partner at GV, who led the investment for the fund', so GV entered at the Series B (the firm's listing first carries Toast in 2016; the IPO-era agreements name GV 2014 and GV 2017 vehicles, and GV filed 13G holdings in 2022-23). Market cap $17.56B on 2026-09-28 (stockanalysis.com), replacing the June 2025 float.

Application performance tracing for distributed web apps, Providence RI. TechCrunch (2011-11-03): a $600,000 seed from Battery Ventures, Flybridge Capital Partners, Google Ventures and angels, the company's first disclosed funding (founded June 2010). Bain Capital Ventures then invested $5.2M in March 2012 (its Form D, per BCV's row), a later priced round above the seed-era $5M bar; AppNeta acquired the company in 2012 (the firm's exit line). Graduation left for the graduation pass. Aligned with BCV's row (acquired, Providence).

Engineering productivity analytics, San Francisco. TechCrunch (2015-04-02): Twitter bought tenXer for under $50M; 'The company had raised about $5 million with investors including True Ventures, Google Ventures and Khosla', with no round named. Google News for the company returned no funding announcement. No source ties GV to a named round, so the stage is undetermined (Khosla's row reads Seed off the same article). Acquired, aligned with Khosla's row (San Francisco).

Personalised news and talk radio app by Concept.io. TechCrunch (2013-07-18): 'Swell previously raised a $1.8 million seed round from Google Ventures, Charles River Ventures, DFJ, Andreessen Horowitz' and others, and a $5.4M Series A 'led by Draper Fisher Jurvetson, with participation from Google Ventures', so GV entered at the seed and the named Series A graduates it. TechCrunch (2014-07-28): Concept.io was 'founded back in 2012 in Mountain View', its seed 'was led by CRV and Andreessen Horowitz in 2012' (the entry date), and Apple bought Swell and its team for about $30M; the app shut down (Fast Company headline). Status and stage align with a16z's row; its city (Palo Alto) differs from the Mountain View this row cites. First Round's 'Swell' (defunct, New York, 2017 listing) is a different company of the same name.

Crowdsourced penetration testing, Redwood City (Wikipedia). Wikipedia: 'In April 2014, the company announced it had secured Series A funding from Kleiner Perkins Caufield Byers, Google Ventures, Allegis Capital, and Derek Smith'; the Business Journals headline gives the round as $7.5M led by Kleiner Perkins (2014-04-24). The firm's listing first carries Synack in 2014 and its /ai list records re-investments in March 2017 and March 2020. Later rounds: $25M Series B (February 2015), $21M (April 2017, Fortune headline), $52M (May 2020, Business Wire headline); no mark near $1B.

Weather insurance, then farm data science (WeatherBill until 2011), San Francisco. TechCrunch (2007-10-17): WeatherBill's $12.5M Series B, led by NEA and Index Ventures. Google Ventures was founded in 2009 (the firm's own 'EST. 2009'), so any GV entry came in a later round: Growth, though no source read names the round or its date (model, medium). Acquired by Monsanto in October 2013 for about $1.1B (Wikipedia; the firm's exit line 'Acquired by Monsanto, 2013'), so below_1b by the acquired-row rule. Aligned with the sibling books (acquired, San Francisco).

AI that automates patient referral intake (faxes, documents) for specialty providers, New York. The company's release (PR Newswire, 2025-06-18): 'a $101 million Series C led by IVP, with participation from new and existing investors including Andreessen Horowitz, Lightspeed, GV, ICONIQ'; the firm's /ai list gives a single 'Invested 2025-06', so GV entered at the Series C: Growth. Fortune's headline puts the round at a $605M valuation. Momentum check 2026-09-28 (Google News for the company): no later round, so below_1b. Aligned with a16z, IVP and Lightspeed (private, New York).

Mobile credit scoring and lending in emerging markets (InVenture until its rename to Tala), headquartered in Santa Monica (Wikipedia, 'Tala Finance'). The pre-filled DZ is a Wikidata join on the one-word name and is disputed. TechCrunch (2014-03-14): 'a $1.2 million seed round led by Chris Sacca's Lowercase Capital. Other investors in that round include Google Ventures'; the firm's 2014 listing names InVenture. Global Venturing (2015-09-22): a $10M Series A 'from a consortium including Google Ventures', so the seed graduated. Later rounds (per Ribbit's row): IVP-led $30M Series B (2017), $145M Series E (2021, enterprise value above $800M); no priced round at $1B found. City: Ribbit says Santa Monica and IVP Los Angeles; Wikipedia gives Santa Monica. Seed date read off the TechCrunch report (March 2014). (Tala Health, the $1.2B AI health startup of 2025, is a different company.)

Dental studio chain (25 locations in New York, Washington DC, Boston, Atlanta, Nashville and Connecticut). Entry: the company's release (New York, 2020-10-01), 'Tend Raises $37M Series B Led By GV': '$37 million in new funding led by GV', with Juxtapose, Redpoint and Zigg named as the existing investors, so GV entered at the Series B: Growth. The Form D band had dated the entry to the 2024 filing where GV's Ben Robbins sits (a follow-on; the firm listed Tend from 2020), so its date is replaced. A $125M Series C followed in April 2021 (Business Insider and Business Journals headlines). HQ: the 2024 Form D gives the issuer and officers at 8 City Boulevard, Nashville, and the company's release naming Troy Bage CEO is datelined Nashville (PR Newswire, 2023-08-14; 'based out of Tend's Nashville hub'); Redpoint's row says New York, this row holds the fresher cited address. Operating (the company's site, 2026); no priced round near $1B.

Crowdsourced search and social advertising marketplace, Boulder. TechCrunch (2010-07-21): 'a $5.75 million Series C round of funding led by Google Ventures, with participation from previous investor Foundry Group', $7.95M raised in total; GV's Rich Miner sits on the July 2010 Form D. The Form D band read that filing as a Seed; the press names it a Series C, so the entry is Growth (band disputed; the seed-to-A column does not apply). A further $9M came in 2011 from Google Ventures and Foundry (Search Engine Land headline). Daily Camera (2015-03-30): the creditors, who held Trada's assets as collateral, 'have forced the provider of paid search advertising services to cease operations'; the firm's live list no longer carries it (archived listings 2012-2015 only): defunct.

Health-budget benefits platform (ICHRA) for employers, San Francisco. The firm's listing gives thatch.ai, which redirects to thatch.com: the same company as General Catalyst's and Lux's Thatch rows. The pre-filled GB is a name join on the one-word name and is disputed (US). Entry: the company's launch release (PR Newswire, San Francisco, 2023-02-15): over $6M across a pre-seed and a seed, and 'The company's seed round was led by a16z and GV' (GV's Krishna Yeshwant quoted); the firm's listing first carries Thatch in 2023. Graduated: General Catalyst's post (2024-09-05) says it is 'co-leading a Series A investment'. Mark: the $108M Series C at a $1B valuation (the company's release, San Francisco, 2026-09-15), led by The General Partnership, Index, General Catalyst and a16z; pinned from the unicorn list's name match. Aligned with General Catalyst ($1B, 2026-09) and Lux (Seed, graduated).

funding_rounds.lead: The General Partnership; Index Ventures; General Catalyst; Andreessen Horowitz

note: AI-native software development platform, London (founder Guy Podjarny of Snyk). The company's release (London, 2024-11-14): $125M in total, a previously unannounced $25M seed of April 2024 led by boldstart ventures and GV, and a $100M Series A led by Index Ventures with Accel, GV and boldstart. The firm's own post (2026-03-18) agrees: 'GV was a seed investor in Tessl in 2024'; its case study gives 'First Round: Seed' and the /ai list 'Invested 2024-04' (the first Form D, $25.5M, is dated 2024-04-10 with Tom Hulme and boldstart's Ed Sim as directors). The Form D band read that filing as a Series A; the release names it the seed, so the band is disputed. The named Series A graduates the seed. Valuation reported at $500M+ (TechCrunch headline) or $750M (Fortune headline): below_1b. Momentum check 2026-09-28 (Google News for the company): no later round.

Marketing intelligence from social media data (Socialgraphics), founded in Boston. The company's release (Marketwire, 2012-12-03) and TechCrunch the same day: a '$1.2 million funding round led by Google Ventures' with Charles River Ventures, Common Angels, 500 Startups, Boston Seed and angels. Neither names the round; a $1.2M round from seed funds and angels is read as the seed (model, medium). Fate: truelens.com now redirects to an unrelated eyewear retailer; vendor profiles list an acquisition by MarketingAudit in 2018, which no non-vendor source read confirms, so status is unknown. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Gallium nitride power semiconductors, Goleta CA (a UCSB spin-out, founded 2007). GV's Wesley Chan sits on the company's first electronic Form D (April 2010, $20.2M) beside Kleiner Perkins' Randy Komisar and Foundation Capital's Richard Redelfs, so GV was in by then; Wikipedia says 'In 2011, Google Ventures invested $20 million'. No source read names the round GV entered (earlier 2007-09 money is on no electronic filing), so the stage is undetermined. Renesas agreed to buy the company for $339M in January 2024 and completed the purchase on 2024-06-20 (Wikipedia): acquired. The firm's exit line ('Acuired by Renesas Electronics, 2020') carries a wrong year. Lux's row still reads public (listed 2020 to 2024); this row holds the completed acquisition.

Precision oncology small molecules and degraders, Watertown MA (the 2024-25 Form Ds; Stamford CT on the 2021-22 filings). Fierce Biotech (2025-09-03): 'Treeline launched in 2021 with a series A led by Arch Venture Partners, GV and OrbiMed', and its later raises were Series A extensions ($261M in 2022 per Crunchbase News, $200M in September 2025); GV's David Schenkein sits on every Form D from the first ($220M, April 2021). The Form D band read that first filing as Growth by size; the record names it the Series A, so the band is disputed. Mark: more than $1B raised but no priced round with a published valuation, so below_1b under Rule A, flagged needs_web_value. Pending: a reverse merger with Standard BioTools announced 2026-06-08 (combined company to trade as TRLN, Standard holders to own 16%, close expected in the second half of 2026; Fierce); Standard BioTools still trades separately on 2026-09-28 (stockanalysis.com), so the deal has not closed and the row stays private.

CRM, itineraries and payments software for independent travel advisors; its terms of use give 2261 Market Street, San Francisco. TechCrunch (2024-03-01): the company raised its seed in 2019 and an unannounced $10M Series A about a year earlier, led by Acrew Capital with NFX, Founder Collective, Forerunner and Concrete Rose (no GV named). The firm lists it from 2019 but no source read ties GV to a named round, so the stage is undetermined (a listing capture does not name the entry). Operating (the company's site, 2026).

Meeting-room and workplace analytics software (EventBoard until its rename), Salt Lake City. Crunchbase News (2020-01): Teem raised about $23M with investors including Greycroft and NGP Capital, was bought by WeWork in September 2018 (reported $100M; the firm's exit line 'Acquired by WeWork, 2018'), and WeWork sold it to iOFFICE (iOFFICE's release, Houston, 2020-01-14, 'Salt Lake City-based Teem'). No source read names the round GV entered (the firm lists it from 2016), so the stage is undetermined. Acquired.

Infrastructure and privileged access management. The company's release (Burlingame, 2021-09-15): a $54M Series B 'led by Tiger Global, with participation from new investor GV' (GV's Erik Nordlander quoted), so GV entered at the Series B: Growth. The $34M Series C release (Palo Alto, 2024-05-02) names GV, Sequoia and True Ventures as existing investors, $96M raised in total. Delinea announced the acquisition in January 2026 and completed it in March 2026 (StrongDM's own About page; GlobeNewswire via Manila Times): acquired. City from the latest release dateline (Palo Alto); Sequoia's row still reads private and San Francisco, this row holds the completed acquisition.

Virtual specialist care for ALS, Parkinson's and dementia patients, Chicago (2045 W Grand Ave). The company's release (Chicago, 2022-02-01): a $6M seed led by GV with LifeForce Capital, Martin Ventures, Byers Capital, Y Combinator and angels. Graduated: the $25M Series A (Chicago, 2024-11-19) was led by B Capital with existing backers Google Ventures, Optum Ventures and Rock Health Capital. Operating (the company's site, 2025-26). Aligned with Y Combinator's row (Chicago).

Automated cryostorage and tracking of frozen eggs and embryos for IVF clinics, New York. The company's release (New York, 2021-07-20): a $105M Series C of equity and debt whose equity 'was led by Transformation Capital and includes participation from GV (formerly Google Ventures)', with 5AM Ventures and Life Sciences Innovation Fund named as the existing investors, so GV entered at the Series C: Growth. Earlier: $12M Series A (2019) and $25M Series B led by 5AM (December 2019); a Series D in July 2024 (the company's newsroom). Reprotech and TMRW announced a business combination on 2026-04-02 (Reprotech's release) and Reprotech now sells TMRW's products; the firm's exit line reads 'Acquired by Reprotech, 2026': acquired.

Marketplace matching substitute teachers with schools, San Francisco. citybiz (2023-06-01): Swing Education, 'a San Francisco, CA-based online marketplace', raised a $38M Series C co-led by Apax Partners and Reach Capital, following 'a 2018 Series B funding co-led by GV (formerly Google Ventures) and Owl Ventures and a seed round' from Social Capital, Kapor, Moment, Ulu and others (no GV), so GV entered at the Series B: Growth (the firm lists it from 2018). A $20M growth loan from Runway Growth followed in August 2025 (PR Newswire headline). Operating (the company's site). Y Combinator's row leaves the city empty.

AI lip-sync and visual dubbing models (sync.so; legal name Synchronicity Labs). The company's own post (2024-08-16): a '$5.5M seed round led by Google Ventures' with Y Combinator, Creator Ventures and Rebel Fund; the firm's /ai list gives 'Invested 2024-04', read as the entry date (D7: the round's post dates the announcement, not the investment). City from knowledge (San Francisco). Momentum check 2026-09-28: Google News for the company returned no later round, so below_1b; the entry is past 24 months, so not censored. Graduation left for the graduation pass. Y Combinator's 'sync.' row (Seoul, KR) describes a different company on the same domain (a one-person Seoul fund, per its own note): a name collision, not aligned.

Neuropsychiatry drugs (schizophrenia, depression), spun out of Israel's Clexio Biosciences. Fierce Biotech (2025-12-18): a $165M Series A led by Dexcel Pharma and Third Rock Ventures, with 'Bain Capital Life Sciences, Google Ventures, QVT and Pictet' participating, at the company's launch; the firm lists it from 2026, so GV entered at the Series A. The company 'is based in Tel Aviv and Boston' (Fierce); its founders are Teva and Clexio veterans in Israel and Calcalist lists the round among Israeli funding rounds, so recorded as Tel Aviv, IL: a judgment call on a two-site company (Boston is the other site).

Therapeutics from somatic mosaicism and clonal hematopoiesis (CHIP). Crunchbase News (2022-01-27): the company 'launched Thursday with a $40 million Series A round funded by Foresite Capital and GV', San Francisco-based, co-founded by Foresite Labs, CEO Mark Chao: GV entered at the launch Series A. Fate unclear: the company's domain (tensixteen.bio) is now a parked page offering it for sale, and an Endpoints piece (2025-05-21, unread, paywalled) reports a new spinout led by a Forty Seven co-founder in the same field; the firm still lists the company. No source read gives its fate, so status is unknown.

Birth-control telehealth and pharmacy delivery. Business Insider (January 2019): 'Investors including GV just put another $51 million' into the company, 'San Carlos, California-based The Pill Club has now raised $67 million from investors including VMG, GV's consumer team, Base10, Shasta Ventures and Acme Capital'; the round is not named and GV's place in the earlier $16M is not given, so the stage is undetermined (the firm lists it from 2019). A $42M round followed in June 2021 (Fierce Healthcare headline). After an $18.3M Medicaid-fraud settlement with California (February 2023) the company filed for bankruptcy (Mercury News headline, April 2023) and Thirty Madison bought its assets in June 2023 (MobiHealthNews, Fierce Healthcare and Business Journals headlines): acquired out of insolvency, with Thirty Madison (Nurx) the successor; thepillclub.com now redirects to Nurx.

Epitope-level target discovery for precision cancer therapies (ADCs), founded 2022. citybiz (2026-04-07): 'Cambridge, Mass.-based Stipple Bio has emerged from stealth' with a $100M Series A co-led by RA Capital, a16z Bio+Health and Nextech, 'with participation from existing investors Emerson Collective ..., GV (Google Ventures), LoLa Capital Partners'. GV was therefore in before the Series A, in one of the unnamed earlier rounds (Form Ds: $12M in 2022, $15M in late 2024), but no source names which, and no GV person sits on any filing. The Form D band had read the 2022 filing (a16z's Vineeta Agarwala its outside director) as GV's Series A entry; the company names the 2026 round its Series A, so that label and its date are withdrawn and the stage is undetermined. City: Cambridge (the release and the 2026 Form D addresses); a16z's row still gives Milford from the 2022 filing.

funding_rounds.lead: RA Capital; a16z Bio+Health; Nextech Invest

note: Athlete-written sports media founded by Derek Jeter, New York. Variety (2017-01-19): 'closed $40 million in Series C funding, led by venture-capital firm IVP. The latest round includes participation from Alphabet's GV (formerly known as Google Ventures), dozens of individual athletes, and existing investors including Thomas Tull ..., New Enterprise Associates, and GenTrust', so GV entered at the Series C: Growth (the firm lists it from 2017). Acquired by Minute Media in November 2019 (Wikipedia; Variety headline; the firm's exit line). Aligned with IVP's row (acquired, New York, Growth).

Antisense and genetic medicines restoring UNC13A for ALS. BioPharma Dive (2024-11-12): the company 'launched Tuesday with $101 million from an investment group that includes Atlas Venture, RA Capital Management and Alphabet's venture capital arm, GV. Third Rock led the round'; ALS News Today and the Business Wire headline name it the Series A. The firm lists it from 2024, so GV entered at the launch Series A. Operating (first clinical program, June 2026, Business Wire headline). Located only as 'the San Francisco area' (BioPharma Dive); no source read names the municipality, so the city is left open.

Robotic cloud laboratory for life-science experiments. Transcriptic merged with 3Scan in 2019 to form Strateos (Y Combinator's row; Strateos raised a $56M Series B in 2021 and shifted to on-site cloud labs in 2023, Business Wire and Fierce headlines); status aligned with Y Combinator's row (acquired, by merger). City: Strateos's contact page lists Menlo Park first (3565 Haven Ave), with San Diego and South San Francisco sites; Y Combinator's row says San Francisco. No source read names the round GV entered (the firm lists the company from 2013, partner Blake Byers), so the stage is undetermined; Google News for the company returned no funding report.

Consumer app distribution for Windows PC makers (Pokki, the OpenCandy network), San Diego with a Seattle office (Wikipedia). Wikipedia: 'SweetLabs has raised at least $21.5 million in venture capital from Bessemer Venture Partners, Google Ventures, Intel Capital, and O'Reilly AlphaTech Ventures'; no source read names the round GV entered (the firm lists it from 2012), so the stage is undetermined. Operating: its site (privacy policy updated 2023) describes an app developer for device makers. No mark near $1B.

Social reading and ebook annotation app used in classrooms, Seattle. Acquired by Renaissance Learning in 2013 (the firm's exit line 'Acquired by Renaissance Learning, 2013'). No source read names the round GV entered (the firm lists it from 2012); Google News for the company returned no funding report, so the stage is undetermined.

Location-based mobile advertising and yield management for local merchants (a TechStars company). Telenav bought it for $22.5M in October 2012 (Business Insider headline; the firm's exit line 'Acquired by Telenav, 2012'), and InMarket acquired Thinknear from Telenav in 2019 (Marketing Dive, 2019-08-09). City from knowledge (Santa Monica). No source read names the round GV entered, so the stage is undetermined.

Heart-disease gene therapies and small molecules (NASDAQ: TNYA), South San Francisco. The company's release (South San Francisco, 2019-10-03): the $92M Series B 'was led by Casdin Capital and included GV, The Column Group', with GV's Anthony Philippakis joining as board observer. GV's only vehicle on the Series C investors' rights agreement (2020-12-17, filed with the S-1) is GV 2019, L.P., so it was not in the Series A (sold through December 2018): GV entered at the Series B, Growth. Market cap $132.25M on 2026-09-28 (stockanalysis.com), replacing the June 2025 float.

Enterprise data mastering and unification, Cambridge MA (co-founded by Michael Stonebraker and Andy Palmer). The company's own releases: the June 2015 round was its $25.2M Series B, with NEA and Google Ventures as existing investors (Cambridge, 2015-06-19), and the $18M round of July 2018 calls 'NEA and GV' its founding investors. GV was therefore in the founding round that preceded the Series B, read as the Series A (model, medium); no source read names that round or dates it (the firm lists Tamr from 2014, and its /ai list records re-investments in 2018, 2020 and 2022). Private, operating; no priced round near $1B.

AAV gene therapies for CNS diseases (NASDAQ: TSHA), Dallas. The S-1 (2020-09-02) names 'GV (formerly Google Ventures)' among the investors in its $126M of preferred stock: a $30M Series A (March to July 2020, almost all to PBM Capital and Nolan Capital) and a $96M Series B (July and August 2020, Fidelity the largest related-party buyer). The related-party tables do not list GV, and no source read says which series it bought, so the stage is undetermined. Market cap $1.63B on 2026-09-28 (stockanalysis.com), replacing the June 2025 float ($545M), so the band moves to 1b_plus.
